ms.promise:
Orcfax will develop a dashboard page on the Orcfax Explorer that utilizes highly informative visualizations to aid users. These new visualizations may include (but are not limited to):
・Orcfax feed price charts (eg ADA-USD)
・state change timelines (eg the life cycle of data)
・data provenance (eg methods for verifying authenticity)
ms.criteria:
This milestone will conclude with the successful passing of all visualization test cases:
・The dashboard must display dynamic price charts which are informed by orcfax feed publications.
・The dashboard must give users the ability to follow each step of the oracle data lifecycle (from collection to publication)
・The dashboard must allow users to verify authenticity through easy to use widgets

ms.promise: Orcfax will develop a new feature for the Orcfax Explorer which allows users to download and read the audit log package for a given fact statement.
ms.criteria:
This milestone will conclude with the successful passing of the audit package download test case:
・A test user must be able to select and download their target audit package.
・The audit package must include a static archive explorer in order to aid in sense-making.
・The static archive explorer should mimic the user experience of the Orcfax Explorer
・The audit package must display the same archival records as the Orcfax explorer in order two allow a test user to corroborate what is seen on the Explorer.
ms.report:
What we promised:
Orcfax will develop a new feature for the Orcfax Explorer which allows users to download and read the audit log package for a given fact statement. These upgrades were to be published on our public Orcfax GitHub along with source code, tests, and user documentation to aid in use.

What we delivered:
The ability for users to download specific fact statements and view them, along with archival information, offline on their own computers! These two new features are now included in the public github explorer repo where we provide additional context and the relevant code enhancements for each.

We have also published the announcement for our explorer feature upgrade on X and Discord.

For test cases, we have recorded a walkthrough of explorer.orcfax.io so that users can see how the new features work in tandem to deliver an incredible Explorer Viewer experience. This walkthrough also serves as a resource for users looking to better understand the upgrades within the context of the explorer UI.

ms.report:
What we promised:
Orcfax will develop new features for the Orcfax Explorer which results in new dynamic displays; the new features will enhance the existing dashboard page on the Orcfax Explorer so that it displays information about Orcfax network activity in real time, including (but not limited to):
 • validator node participation statistics
 • network health.
These upgrades were to be published on our public Orcfax GitHub along with source code, tests, and user documentation to aid in use.

What we delivered:
The new feature set for the explorer brings the following changes:

・The dashboard now has a section which dynamically displays statistics relating to node participation 
・Identifies when each node last published.
・Identifies the feed each node last published to.
・Identifies the total number of publications (i.e. Facts) for each node.
・Provides the status/health of each node.

These two new features are now included in the public github explorer repo where we provide additional context and the relevant code enhancements for each. These changes have also been documented on in our docs.

For test cases, we have recorded a walkthrough of explorer.orcfax.io so that users can see how the new features work in tandem to deliver an incredible Explorer Viewer experience. This walkthrough also serves as a resource for users looking to better understand the upgrades within the context of the explorer UI.

ms.promise: Orcfax will develop a new Orcfax Explorer feature which notifies users in the event of a network issue, and provides users with links to incident reports.
ms.criteria:
This milestone will conclude with creation of documentation which explains how incidents are recorded and reported in the Orcfax Explorer, and with the successful passing of the network incident-reporting test cases:
・The system must provide real time notifications of network related incidents
・A test user must be able to use a network incident notification to navigate to a formal report of the incident
ms.report:
What we promised:
Orcfax will develop a new Orcfax Explorer feature which notifies users in the event of a network issue, and provides users with links to incident reports.
These upgrades were to be published on our public Orcfax GitHub along with source code, tests, and user documentation to aid in use.

What we delivered:
The new feature set for the explorer brings the following changes:
・Adds a landing page to a Status Dashboard with key statistics: https://github.com/orcfax/status.orcfax.io/issues/3
・Adds “Incidents” to Status Dashboard
・Adds “Network Updates” to Status Dashboard
・Adds an RSS Feed Url Builder to Status Dashboard
・Allows Orcfax to Serve Orcfax RSS Feed from Status App
・Provides an index of Sources for the Orcfax RSS Feed

These two new features are now included in the public github explorer repo where we provide additional context and the relevant code enhancements for each. These changes have also been documented on in our docs.

For test cases, we have recorded a walkthrough of explorer.orcfax.io so that users can see how the new features work in tandem to deliver an incredible Explorer Viewer experience. This walkthrough also serves as a resource for users looking to better understand the upgrades within the context of the explorer UI.
